text:
**Short answer:** for a typical full-size fridge, about 1,000 Wh covers most of a day, and 1,400-2,000 Wh covers a full 24 hours with some margin. The inverter needs a surge rating of at least ~1,300 W (up to ~2,400 W for big or older fridges) and pure sine wave output.

**The three checks**
1. **Continuous watts:** a full-size fridge runs at roughly 100-250 W, which almost any 1,000 W-class station handles ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
2. **Surge watts:** the compressor spikes at startup, about 1,000-1,800 W for a top-freezer and 1,500-2,400 W for a large French-door or older unit ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)). This is the spec that most often blocks a fridge, and a big battery won't help if the surge rating is too low ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
3. **Watt-hours:** the compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so average draw is far below the label wattage.
   - One guide estimates ~1,400 Wh per day (41 W average, with losses and 20% headroom) and ~2,800 Wh for two days ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
   - Another estimates about 62 Wh per hour, so a ~1,000 Wh unit runs ~17 hours ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).

For a more exact number, take your fridge's EnergyGuide kWh/year, multiply by 1,000 and divide by 8,760 to get average watts. Then multiply by outage hours and add ~40% for losses and margin. Keeping the door shut stretches runtime.

**Sizing by outage length**
- **Up to ~12-16 hours:** ~1,000 Wh, such as the [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/) (1,070 Wh, listed around $499). The Bluetti AC180 (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W with 2,700 W peak) is listed at $399-699 on [BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage).
- **A full day or more:** ~2,000 Wh.
  - [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l): 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, expandable to 8 kWh. It's $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF. This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you, and the store's checkout price is the final word.
   - [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator): 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W with 3,000 W peak, listed at $699.99 after coupon.
- **Multi-day outages:** 3,000 Wh or more, or an expandable unit you can pair with solar.

Whatever you buy, confirm the surge rating clears your fridge's startup draw. Check the manual or ask the manufacturer, and add any other devices you'll run at the same time.

If you tell me your fridge's size and model, how long your outages usually last, and your budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
